claim.why_it_matters: The heading is invisible to the outline and to any tool that locates clauses by heading, so citations to §1985:IX.1.3.x cannot be resolved to this text by structure.
claim.detail: Printed as a numbered subsection heading (sibling of 1.3.1 Organization, which the markdown on page 471 renders as `#### 1.3.1 Organization`); the markdown renders it as a plain paragraph line with no heading marker, so it drops out of the document outline. The Relative I-O module renders the same heading as `### 1.3.2 Access Modes`.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 472 (IX-2, Indexed I-O - Introduction) prints '1.3.2 Access Modes' as a numbered subsection heading on its own line, set off like 1.3.3 and 1.3.4. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 18452 it is the bare line '1.3.2 Access Modes' with no heading marker, while its sibling at line 18438 is '#### 1.3.1 Organization' and the Relative I-O module renders the same headings as '### 1.3.2/1.3.3/1.3.4' (lines 17182-17194). The text is intact, so meaning is unchanged; the defect is structural (outline/heading lookup), as claimed. The same defect also affects '1.3.3 File Position Indicator' (line 18460) and '1.3.4 I-O Status' (line 18464) on this same page.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate for 1.3.2 Access Modes; the same missing heading marker also applies to its siblings 1.3.3 File Position Indicator and 1.3.4 I-O Status on page 472 (markdown lines 18452, 18460, 18464), all three of which should be headings at the level of '#### 1.3.1 Organization'.
